post.title: Why companies pay the agencies that grade their debt
post.ig:
Companies pay the agencies that grade their own debt. It's called issuer-pays.
S&P Global Ratings: $4,724M revenue and $3,013M operating profit in 2025, a 64% margin (FY2025 10-K).
Moody's Investors Service revenue: $4.12B in 2025, up 9% (FY2025).
S&P, Moody's and Fitch held 93.38% of ratings outstanding from SEC-registered agencies at the end of 2024 (SEC staff report).
Accused of inflating pre-crisis mortgage ratings, S&P settled for $1.375B in 2015 and Moody's for $864M in 2017; neither settlement found a violation of law.
Sources: S&P Global and Moody's FY2025 10-Ks, SEC 2025 Staff Report on NRSROs, DOJ and company releases.
News and education, not financial advice.

Under the issuer-pays model, companies pay S&P, Moody's and Fitch to grade their debt. S&P Global Ratings earned $3,013M operating profit on $4,724M revenue in 2025 (64% margin), and Moody's ratings revenue hit $4.12B; the big three held 93.38% of SEC-registered agency ratings at the end of 2024 per the SEC. Sources: FY2025 10-Ks, SEC 2025 Staff Report on NRSROs, 2015 and 2017 settlement releases. News and education, not financial advice.
